articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 security patches including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw called 'BlueHammer' - because apparently Redmond's idea of spring cleaning is patching vulnerabilities by the gross.

articles.title: Clavicular and the Right-Wing Project to Radicalize Young Men
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability gets weaponized faster than you can say 'shared hosting nightmare' - researchers claim zero-day activity for at least a month before disclosure because responsible disclosure is apparently dead.

articles.title: Real estate giant confirms vishing incident as ShinyHunters and Qilin both come knocking
articles.summary: Fresh 'CopyFail' Linux kernel bug gets exploited within days of researchers dropping a working root exploit - proving once again that the time between 'oops' and 'owned' keeps shrinking.

articles.title: DAEMON Tools Supply Chain Attack Compromises Official Installers with Malware
articles.summary: Apache HTTP/2 serves up a critical flaw (CVE-2026-23918) with potential RCE because the foundation that runs half the internet apparently had one job and briefly forgot how to do it.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs Top 34 Prospects
articles.summary: Wiz researchers unearth 20-year-old PostgreSQL vulnerabilities in pgcrypto - because nothing says 'enterprise database security' like decades-old crypto bugs hiding in plain sight.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military hackers mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens through compromised routers because why break into one system when you can steal authentication for thousands at once.

articles.title: China-Linked UAT-8302 Targets Governments Using Shared APT Malware Across Regions
articles.summary: DAEMON Tools suffers supply chain attack with compromised installers distributed from their own website - because apparently even legitimate digital certificates can't save you from getting pwned at the source.

articles.title: Your work apps are quietly handing 19 data points to someone
articles.summary: 15-year-old French kid allegedly breaches government agency exposing 12-18 million records - proving that age is just a number when it comes to embarrassing state cybersecurity.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: EFF rallies against the 'turnkey totalitarian state' built by surveillance architecture - because William Binney warned us and apparently we're still not listening hard enough.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SIM-swapping spree - another reminder that cybercrime groups have better operational security than most Fortune 500 companies.
